assertion.name: Prdm16 cardiomyocyte-specific knockout mouse (Prdm16cKO)
assertion.genotype: Prdm16 conditional knockout, cardiomyocyte-restricted via Xmlc2-Cre and, independently, cTnT-Cre (both lines called Prdm16cKO in the paper)
assertion.description: Conditional deletion of Prdm16 restricted to cardiomyocytes. assertion.name: Cardiac-specific Prdm16 conditional knockout mouse (conduction and fibrosis phenotype)
assertion.genotype: Cardiac-specific Prdm16 conditional knockout via alpha-MHC (Myh6)-Cre (Prdm16-null hearts); the driver is not named in this paper's own abstract-only record here and is attributed by PMID:37395136, which identifies its model as similar to Nam et al's Myh6-Cre knockout
assertion.description: Cardiac-restricted Prdm16 null model phenotyped by electrocardiography, fibrosis histology and left ventricular RNA sequencing. It is the only model in this entry that measures TGF-beta pathway activity in vivo and then tests it pharmacologically: TGF-beta signaling is activated in Prdm16-null hearts, but blocking the TGF-beta receptor does not rescue the conduction defect. That negative rescue result separates the fibrotic and conduction arms of the mechanism, and the accompanying ion-channel transcript dysregulation offers a TGF-beta-independent route to the arrhythmia node.

modeled_mechanisms.description: TGF-beta signaling is activated in Prdm16-null hearts at both ligand transcript and downstream effector level, the direction predicted by PRDM16 acting as a repressor of TGFB transcription.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: This model's direction conflicts with the Prdm16Q187X heterozygote, which shows age-dependent loss of TGF-beta expression. The two differ in allele class (complete cardiac null versus a heterozygous nonsense variant), dose and timepoint. The Q187X paper proposes that PRDM16 regulates TGF-beta bidirectionally in a temporally-dependent manner, which would make the two findings phases of one mechanism; that has not been tested across models, so the sign of the TGF-beta change in human LVNC8 should not be inferred from either model alone. The driver is alpha-MHC (Myh6)-Cre, attributed by PMID:37395136 rather than stated in this paper's own record here, and it matters: Myh6-Cre knockouts are reported to give hypertrophy in one model and LV dilation in another, and a later paper judged the earlier conditional Prdm16 lines not to mirror the patient LVNC phenotype.

assertion.genotype: Prdm16lox/lox;Sm22alpha-Cre (called Prdm16cKO in the paper), deleting Prdm16 exon 9 in cardiomyocytes from early cardiac development onward

assertion.name: Hypoglycin A and MCPA immersion in zebrafish embryos and larvae
assertion.description: Wild-type AB embryos were exposed by immersion beginning at 24 hours after fertilization, with monitoring through 96 hours. HGA and MCPA produced mortality, bradycardia and cardiac edema, with later toxicity onset after HGA; MCPA also reduced swimming under selected exposure conditions. The model was developed for Sapindaceae-associated equine atypical myopathy and captures shared toxin biology rather than human ackee ingestion or a demonstrated human hypoglycemic syndrome. Whole-body metabolite and locomotor experiments each had one experimental replicate; metabolomics pooled twenty larvae per concentration. Mortality assays used biological triplicates. Glycine and carnitine co-exposure reduced 72-hour mortality, whereas riboflavin did not protect in this protocol. Compounds were added simultaneously with toxin, so this is prevention/co-treatment evidence, not treatment after established poisoning. Surviving larvae could retain cardiac abnormalities. MCPrG caused no observed toxicity in this exposure system, but uptake and activation were unresolved; the result does not establish safety in mammals.

modeled_mechanisms.description: HGA-exposed larvae accumulated the downstream conjugate MCPA-carnitine.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Indirect bioactivation readout from pooled whole-body material with no biological replicate series; neither MCPA-CoA nor a specific activating enzyme was directly quantified. Immersion differs from oral human exposure.

assertion.description: A spontaneous recessive missense allele in the N-terminal RCC1-like domain that raises mutant HERC1 protein levels and lowers mTOR activity, causing autophagy-associated progressive Purkinje cell degeneration with ataxia from the second month, reduced growth and lifespan. Before Purkinje cell loss the mice already show impaired neuromuscular transmission, peripheral myelin abnormalities, fewer presynaptic vesicles, absent amygdalar LTP, and deficits in associative and spatial learning. Transgenic rescue with human HERC1 cDNA validated the locus.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Reproduces progressive, autophagy-associated Purkinje cell loss, but through an allele whose molecular effect (protein accumulation, reduced mTOR, excess autophagy) is the reverse of the human gain-of-function family and different from the human null alleles.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Gly483Glu is an RCC1-like-domain missense allele with increased protein and decreased mTOR activity, whereas human disease alleles are protein nulls or a HECT-domain gain of function with mTORC1 hyperactivation and reduced autophagy; the mouse is not macrocephalic and shows reduced rather than increased growth.

divergences.description: The human initiating lesions (complete loss of HERC1 protein, or a HECT-domain gain of function) are absent from the model; the tambaleante allele accumulates mutant protein and lowers mTOR activity, the opposite direction on the growth-signaling axis.

Mouse Purkinje cell loss begins in adult life and produces ataxia with reduced growth; the human disorder is a congenital overgrowth and neurodevelopmental syndrome in which cerebellar atrophy is reported in a single proband.

assertion.name: Hungarian Vizsla cerebellar cortical degeneration (natural SNX14 model)
assertion.genotype: Homozygous canine SNX14 c.2653+1G>A (CanFam3.1 chr12:45,530,566); p.Gly885Aspfs*16 predicted from aberrant RNA
assertion.description: Two Hungarian Vizsla littermates developed rapidly progressive cerebellar ataxia at two to three months. Both had extensive Purkinje-cell loss, secondary granule-layer depletion and gliosis, with relative caudoventral sparing. MRI in one dog showed mild cerebellar changes. Cerebellar RNA from one case demonstrated a 275-base extension of exon 26; Western blot with an antibody targeting sequence upstream of the splice defect detected neither full-length nor shortened SNX14. The allele is strongly supported as causal, but parental genotypes were unavailable. The dogs were euthanized young, limiting assessment of later manifestations.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Spontaneous, early-onset progressive cerebellar ataxia with primary Purkinje-neuron loss and cerebellar atrophy, driven by SNX14 loss of function as in human SCAR20.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Two juvenile siblings with a rapid course and early euthanasia. No distinctive facial differences were seen. Hearing appeared normal on examination, but auditory electrophysiology was not performed; cognition was difficult to assess and later manifestations could not be excluded. The model therefore does not establish absence of the human syndromic features.

assertion.name: Tecpr2 L1152Yfs knock-in mouse

assertion.description: A second, allele-specific mouse, generated to address a stated limitation of the knockout: a null cannot test whether a truncated mutant TECPR2 protein is itself toxic. The knock-in carries an HSAN9-associated nonsense allele rather than a deletion. It reproduces gait ataxia and the medullary axonal dystrophy seen in the knockout, and it is the source of the endolysosomal and microglial arm of this pathograph: proteomics and imaging of the affected medulla, damage-associated microglia with reduced clearance capacity, and a HOPS interaction mapped in TECPR2 knockout cells.

modeled_mechanisms.target: Endolysosomal Dysfunction and Impaired Microglial Clearance
modeled_mechanisms.description: The model that establishes this node. Neuronal and microglial readouts converge on a dysfunctional endolysosomal system, and the HOPS interaction supplies the molecular basis.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Two limits bound what this model shows. And the design intent was only partly met: the knock-in was made so a truncated mutant protein could be tested for toxic gain-of-function, but TECPR2 was undetectable at the protein level, so functionally this remains a loss-of-expression model like the knockout.

value.name: Lmx1a and Lmx1b central auditory allelic series
value.genotype: Lmx1a drJ functional null with Lmx1b null alleles; Lmx1a-/-, Lmx1a-/-;Lmx1b+/-, double heterozygotes and controls

Roof-plate Bmp6 expression and Atoh1-positive progenitors were reduced at embryonic stages. P0/P14 apoptosis staining did not increase, without excluding other ages. assertion.name: Nrcam knockout mouse
assertion.genotype: Nrcam-null (homozygous knockout)
assertion.description: Constitutive Nrcam-null mice reproduce the cellular defects of the disorder — delayed and abnormal node of Ranvier formation with delayed sodium channel clustering, failure of cerebellar granule cells to extend neurites on contactin-1, excess dendritic spines with increased mEPSC frequency in visual cortex, thalamic axon mistargeting with abnormal visual-evoked potentials, lens fibre disorganization with cataract, and transient cochlear innervation errors — yet do not develop a neuromuscular disorder and have only mildly reduced cerebellar size. The disconnect is the central translational caveat for this entry.

modeled_mechanisms.target: Defective Node of Ranvier Assembly and Maintenance
modeled_mechanisms.description: Peripheral nerves of Nrcam-deficient mice show delayed or abnormal node formation with delayed nodal sodium channel clustering, the same lesion proposed to underlie the human peripheral neuropathy.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Node formation is delayed rather than abolished, because gliomedin provides a partially redundant glial clustering signal; the severe nodal phenotype requires loss of both molecules.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Despite the nodal defect, Nrcam-null mice show no neuromuscular disorder, in contrast to the hypotonia, spasticity and neuropathy present in every reported affected individual.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Probable compensation by other L1-family Ig-CAMs (L1cam, Chl1, Nfasc) in mouse, and possible transcriptional adaptation triggered by nonsense-mediated decay of the null allele. Species differences in the protein itself are also implicated: the KGE and RNRR motifs of the human third Fn-III domain are poorly conserved outside mammals.

modeled_mechanisms.target: Impaired Synaptogenesis and Dendritic Spine Remodeling
modeled_mechanisms.description: NrCAM-null cortex shows elevated dendritic spine density, increased asymmetric synapses and increased mEPSC frequency, establishing NrCAM as a postnatal regulator of spine density within the Sema3F receptor complex.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Measured in mouse primary visual cortex; no corresponding measurement exists in tissue from affected individuals, so the relevance to the human cognitive and behavioural phenotype is inferred.

readouts.name: Apical dendritic spine density on star pyramidal cells
readouts.target: Impaired Synaptogenesis and Dendritic Spine Remodeling
readouts.interpretation: Loss of NrCAM removes Sema3F-dependent spine pruning, raising spine density.

readouts.name: Miniature EPSC frequency in star pyramidal neurons
readouts.target: Impaired Synaptogenesis and Dendritic Spine Remodeling
readouts.interpretation: Functional correlate of the excess excitatory synapses.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Nrcam-null mice reproduce the developmental miswiring — thalamic axon mistargeting to visual cortex with abnormal VEPs, and cochlear afferent and efferent innervation errors — but the cochlear defects self-correct and adult auditory acuity is normal, unlike the persistent hearing impairment in some affected individuals.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Transient cochlear phenotype with functional recovery by weaning; humans appear to lack the compensatory mechanism.

selected_evidence.snippet: In addition, while KO mice have delayed nodes of Ranvier formation and subsequently delayed sodium channel clustering at nodes, they do not exhibit signs of a neuromuscular disorder.

assertion.name: Zebrafish nrcama third Fn-III domain deletion mutant
assertion.genotype: nrcamaΔ (CRISPR-Cas9 deletion of the third Fn-III domain)
assertion.description: A CRISPR-Cas9 mutant deleting the third Fn-III repeat — the domain in which most human disease variants cluster — generated in the founding study. Mutant larvae are viable with no gross morphological defect but show significantly altered swimming behaviour and a trend toward increased α-tubulin fibre density in the dorsal telencephalon and a thickened anterior telencephalic commissure. It is the only in vivo model built around the human variant hotspot.

modeled_mechanisms.target: Aberrant CNS White Matter Tract Formation
modeled_mechanisms.description: Altered axonal projections in the dorsal telencephalon and anterior commissure, the zebrafish counterpart of the mammalian pallium and of the commissural tracts abnormal on human MRI.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The axonal differences were reported as trends and did not reach significance; the pallium is massively expanded in humans relative to zebrafish; and the KGE and RNRR motifs of the human third Fn-III domain are not conserved in zebrafish Nrcam (HGD and QDYD), so the deleted domain is not functionally equivalent.

selected_evidence.snippet: Our studies on zebrafish nrcamaΔ mutants lacking the third Fn-III domain revealed that mutant larvae displayed significantly altered swimming behavior compared to wild-type larvae (p < 0.03).

value.name: Nrcam knockout mouse
value.genotype: Nrcam-null (homozygous knockout)
value.description: Constitutive Nrcam-null mice reproduce the cellular defects of the disorder — delayed and abnormal node of Ranvier formation with delayed sodium channel clustering, failure of cerebellar granule cells to extend neurites on contactin-1, excess dendritic spines with increased mEPSC frequency in visual cortex, thalamic axon mistargeting with abnormal visual-evoked potentials, lens fibre disorganization with cataract, and transient cochlear innervation errors — yet do not develop a neuromuscular disorder and have only mildly reduced cerebellar size. The disconnect is the central translational caveat for this entry.

value.target: Impaired Synaptogenesis and Dendritic Spine Remodeling
value.description: NrCAM-null cortex shows elevated dendritic spine density, increased asymmetric synapses and increased mEPSC frequency, establishing NrCAM as a postnatal regulator of spine density within the Sema3F receptor complex.
value.limitations: Measured in mouse primary visual cortex; no corresponding measurement exists in tissue from affected individuals, so the relevance to the human cognitive and behavioural phenotype is inferred.

value.name: Gliomedin/NrCAM double knockout mouse
value.genotype: Gldn-null; Nrcam-null double knockout
value.description: Removing both glial nodal adhesion molecules abolishes the glial clustering signal entirely and, unlike either single knockout, produces progressive disintegration of established nodes — sequential loss of neurofascin-186, sodium channels, ankyrin-G and then βIV spectrin, binary node formation and dysregulated nodal gap length — with neurological abnormality and slowed nerve conduction. It is the model that isolates the consequences of losing NrCAM-dependent nodal contact from the redundancy that masks them in the single mutant.

value.target: Peripheral Nerve Conduction Failure and Axonal Degeneration
value.description: Loss of the gliomedin/NrCAM clustering signal produces measurable slowing of nerve conduction and neurological abnormality.
value.limitations: The double knockout removes a redundant partner that is intact in affected individuals, so the model overstates the nodal deficit expected from NRCAM loss alone; it establishes the direction of the mechanism rather than its magnitude in human disease.
